title: When the Vow Falls
premise: Ada Sterling has spent a decade planning other people's perfect weddings while refusing her own heart, convinced love is a discipline you can out-train. Her certainty cracks when her reclusive new neighbor, Elian Marsh, is revealed as the anonymous pen pal whose letters have sustained her through her darkest years — letters he wrote as penance, because his testimony once destroyed her father. As Ada's biggest wedding of the season collapses around her and Elian's illness quietly worsens, she must choose between the justice she was raised to demand and the love she swore she'd never risk, learning that forgiveness is a vow you make to yourself before you can make it to anyone else.
about_author: Mara Vane is the pen name of a former wedding coordinator turned novelist who spent six years writing love stories she claimed not to believe in. She lives in a coastal town where she still attends weddings, strictly as a guest, strictly with tissues.

chapters.title: The Muscle and the Machine
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She runs a flawless wedding with surgical precision, then goes home to an empty flat and her ritual of rereading one anonymous letter from a decade of correspondence. Establishes her creed: the heart is trainable, containable. Beat: controlled loneliness disguised as control.

chapters.title: The Man Who Moved In Wrong
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Elian Marsh moves in next door — gruff, guarded, allergic to small talk. Their first encounters are small collisions: a shared stairwell, a borrowed ladder, a ruined batch of her mother's recipe. Beat: friction that neither will admit is fascination.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Unsigned Paper
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, with letter excerpts. We learn the letters began the year her father was convicted after a star witness's testimony, and the anonymous writer has been her only confessor since. She's never known the name. Beat: the ache of being deeply known by a stranger.

chapters.title: A Contract with No Vows in It
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She lands the career-defining commission: a society wedding for a client who wants 'perfection without sentiment' — a mirror of Ada herself. Elian, watching from his window, sketches her working. Beat: Ada mistakes being needed for being safe.

chapters.title: The Neighbor Who Knows My Coffee
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Elian's chapters reveal his secret: he is the letter writer, dying of a heart condition, moved here deliberately to finally face Ada. His small kindnesses — the right coffee, a mended fence — unnerve her. Beat: intimacy arriving before permission.

chapters.title: What the Witness Never Said
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. Flashback to the trial: he testified under pressure, half-truths, a prosecutor's promise. He has carried the letters as penance. His doctor gives him a timeline he refuses to write down. Beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Rain on the Fire Escape
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A storm traps Ada and Elian under one awning; the conversation turns unexpectedly honest — grief, fathers, the weddings she can't attend anymore. She laughs for the first time in months and hates how good it feels. Beat: the first crack in the armor.

chapters.title: The Client Who Wants a Lie
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The society bride demands a fabricated love story for the press; Ada, who sells beautiful surfaces for a living, hesitates for the first time. Elian challenges her: 'You plan vows. Do you think any of them are true?' Beat: her creed publicly questioned.

chapters.title: Letters I Never Sent
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. He drafts a confession letter and burns it. Instead he leaves Ada an unsigned note in their old shared code — and watches her face change through her window. She knows the handwriting. Beat: the secret straining at its seams.

chapters.title: The Archive in the Attic
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Searching for a client's vintage décor, Ada finds her mother's old trial clippings — and a photo of the young star witness. She doesn't recognize him. The reader does. Beat: dramatic irony tightening like a wire.

chapters.title: Two Truths at One Table
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A neighborhood dinner forces Ada and Elian together; the warmth is undeniable, and so is his evasiveness about his past. Ada's mother visits and freezes at the sight of Elian — she recognizes him. Beat: the past knocking at the door.

chapters.title: The Name in the Margins
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Her mother confronts Ada: 'That man testified against your father.' Ada, reeling, cross-checks the handwriting against her letters. It matches. Beat: betrayal — the person she was falling for is the person she was taught to hate.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Stairwell
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She confronts Elian with the letters. He doesn't deny it — he wrote every one, as penance, because the truth he withheld could have freed her father. Ada walks out mid-sentence. Beat: heartbreak weaponized into fury.

chapters.title: The Wedding That Isn't a Wedding
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The society wedding implodes — the bride elopes, the venue cancels, and Ada must salvage a day built entirely on lies. Working eighteen-hour days, she realizes she's using work to stop thinking about Elian. Beat: the armor failing at its job.

chapters.title: What My Father Actually Said
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, visiting her father in prison. She asks about the trial; he admits he begged Elian to testify — and that Elian later sent money to the family anonymously. Her father's version of justice is quieter than her mother's. Beat: the ground shifting under her rage.

chapters.title: The Hospital Corridor
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Elian collapses; a neighbor calls Ada because she's his emergency contact — he listed her years ago, from afar. At his bedside she finds a folder: the full testimony he never gave, and a letter beginning 'If you're reading this, I ran out of time.' Beat: terror masquerading as anger.

chapters.title: The Testimony He Withheld
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, reading the folder. The suppressed evidence could reopen her father's case. She must decide: pursue justice through the courts and lose precious weeks of Elian's time, or stay at his bedside. Beat: justice and love pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Vow I Never Planned
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Elian wakes; Ada, instead of rage, asks him to help her finish the testimony. Working together through the night, they rebuild the truth page by page — the most intimate act either has ever performed. Beat: love redefined as collaboration, not surrender.

chapters.title: Reopening the Case
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. They file the motion; Ada's mother must face her own decade of bitterness, and the family fractures along the fault line of forgiveness. Elian's health deteriorates as the date approaches. Beat: the cost of doing right, paid in advance.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, courtroom scenes. Elian, oxygen tank beside him, testifies at last — the full truth, ten years late. Her father's conviction is overturned. Justice arrives outside the tidy timelines Ada once planned for a living. Beat: catharsis, earned and unsentimental.

chapters.title: Time, Running Out
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. With the case won, Elian tries to push Ada away to spare her grief; she refuses, choosing the whole heart over the safe pieces — even knowing how the story likely ends. They stop counting time and start spending it. Beat: the vow, finally spoken, with no wedding in sight.

chapters.title: When the Vow Falls
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, epilogue a year later. Her father is free; Ada plans weddings again — but only ones she believes in. Elian, post-treatment and fragile but present, waits at the end of an aisle she built herself, for a ceremony with no contract, no performance, just two people keeping the vow they made in a hospital corridor. Beat: love as a promise kept daily, not a single perfect day.
